title.en: The Potter's Canvas: Ceramics and Painting in the 20th Century

events.description: This exhibition looks at how 20th-century British ceramicists used drawing, painting and mark-making to transform the surface of clay. While often regarded as a sculptural medium, many artists also saw clay as their canvas. Pioneer studio potters used minimal, elegant brushwork to enhance form but, as the 20th century progressed, decoration took on new significance, becoming an important part of the making process and a way to convey ideas and subvert expectations. By pairing ceramics from the Shipley Art Gallery with paintings and prints from the Hatton Gallery for the first time, the exhibition examines how the worlds of ceramics and painting shaped each other. The exhibition features over 70 works, highlighting the exceptional quality and range of the Shipley’s collections with ceramics by Bernard Leach, Michael Cardew, Lucie Rie, Hans Coper, James Tower, Gordon Baldwin, Carol McNicoll, Alison Britton, Stephen Dixon and Philip Eglin, alongside paintings and prints from the Hatton’s collection by Patrick Heron, William Scott, Adrian Heath and Victor Pasmore. The exhibition will include key works on loan from the Laing Art Gallery such as a vase by Elizabeth Fritsch and a still life by Winifred Nicholson. Image: Boursa by James Tower, 1984, earthenware with tin-glaze. Shipley Art Gallery, purchased with funding from Northern Arts.

Over time, several reproductions of the Bayeux Tapestry have been made. However, only rarely have copies been complete and to scale. One of the rarer, full-scale copies was created here in Newcastle. Commissioned in the early 1850s by John Collingwood Bruce, this facsimile was created by pupils at Bruce’s school, Percy Street Academy, Newcastle. In 1884, it was donated to the Society of Antiquaries of Newcastle (SANT) where it lay hidden until the early 1990s when it was re-discovered. Bruce's copy is a larger scale than the original and is 5m longer. The drawing is largely complete, with only two sections missing. The copy is currently in 35 separate rolls. On display in this exhibition are four of these sections, showing key parts of the story. Bayeux Around Britain: a British Museum partnership, supported by WorldQuant. Slater began carving out her witty yet pointed take on protest music with her debut EP, ‘You Can’t Put A Price On Fun’, in 2024, which was swiftly followed up with ‘Love Me Please’ the following year. Both projects showcase her undeniable skill as a lyricist, introduce her as a promising new voice in indie rock, and see her take hold of a torch lit by great British songwriters before her – those who have also woven gold from the bleak circumstances of their own generations. events.description: For over a decade, Gotts Street Park have been refining something increasingly rare: music made entirely in the room, by human hands, guided by instinct and friendship. Formed in Leeds by Josh Crocker (bass & production), Tom Henry (keys) and Joe Harris (guitar), the trio have built a distinctive sound rooted in vintage soul and alt-R&B. Earning over 65 million streams on Spotify, the trio collaborate closely with a wide range of vocalists, including Celeste, Rosie Lowe & Olive Jones. What began as a love of sixties Motown has evolved into a genre-spanning catalogue - from the cinematic Diego EP to a growing body of collaborative releases that continue to expand their world. With new music arriving this year, Gotts Street Park are entering their most expansive phase yet. In 2026, that world moves further onto the stage - from debut US performances at Newport Jazz and Montreal to their biggest headline show at London’s Roundhouse - inviting more people than ever into the room with them.

events.description: Its great to have Nashville based country singer/songwriter Jaimee Harris finally come here as the headliner, after so many awesome shows with Mary Gauthier, over the years. Jaimee also comes with a brand new album “Boomerang Town” . She began cultivating Boomerang Town in 2016, a time of great loss for many in the Americana community, with the songwriter losing several musicians close to her. A shift in the nation’s political landscape had ushered in a new level of cultural polarisation and for someone who grew up in a small town outside of Waco, Texas, Harris believed the values instilled by her parents were not entirely in line with how many were viewing, and vilifying, Christians. As a person in recovery, Harris has had to re-evaluate her own connection to faith and find strength in a higher power. It was from the intersection of these social, personal, and political currents that the album was born. While themes of addiction and grief permeate sections of the record, it echoes hope in the face of the darkness. Out this spring, Boomerang Town understands that love and grief are two sides of the same coin.

events.description: Davon Bryant-Mason, aka dreamcastmoe, is a DC-based singer, songwriter, producer, and DJ known for his genre-blurring fusion of R&B, funk, soul, hip-hop, and electronic music. Rooted in the vibrant culture of his hometown, his music reflects the complexity of the city’s rhythms and his own life experiences. From his early SoundCloud days to his acclaimed 2022 debut on Ghostly International’s Spectral Sound, Sound Is Like Water, dreamcastmoe has gained recognition for his soulful storytelling and versatility. A natural performer with a DJ’s knack for live energy, dreamcastmoe’s projects are as dynamic as his sound. Whether honoring his roots with the heartfelt Molly’s Son EP or showcasing his slow-jam finesse on singles like "Next 2 Me," he explores themes of growth, resilience, and joy. His voice—equally adept at falsetto crooning or swaggering talk-rap—ties his eclectic influences into a cohesive vision. For dreamcastmoe, music is both personal and communal, a reflection of his DC heritage and a platform for pushing boundaries while staying grounded in empathy and authenticity.

events.description: Donald Jenkins: Still Raving in Your 40's? Rave tales from the sweaty Underbelly Should middle age really stop you from being a raving reprobate? Still Raving In Your 40’s? is an emotional, euphoric and laugh‑out‑loud spoken‑word and music theatre show that dives headfirst into rave culture, aging, identity and survival on the dancefloor. Through razor‑sharp storytelling, raw honesty and high‑energy delivery, Donald Jenkins takes audiences on a journey from sweaty warehouse raves to the realities of adulthood — without losing the pulse, humour or heart of the underground scene. This is a show for anyone who ever danced until sunrise… and anyone who wonders if they still can. Pete the Temp:. Romantics, Mystics and Revolutionaries A true story of riot, anti-slavery, mysticism and psychedelics; told through the lives of two poet renegades: Samuel Taylor Coleridge and William Wordsworth. The Romantic movement was an act of defiance against industry and the mechanisation of the soul. What do their dreams of renewal offer our age of despair? Part storytelling stage-show, part performance lecture, Pete unfolds a journey of music, comedy and lyricism in a thrilling collision of scholarship and live entertainment. Expect reverence, resistance and enchantment from a time of slavery and war.

events.description: When Bleech 9:3 songwriters/guitarists Barry Quinlan and Sam Duffy first crossed paths in their early twenties, it almost seemed inconceivable that they hadn’t met before. Throughout their tumultuous teenage years spent gigging in various projects around Dublin, they’d lived near-parallel lives mired by the chaos-purgatory spiral of addiction; like two shadows cast by the same light but never touching. In the throes of the early stages of recovery – when a better life still felt elusive and intangible, something to be hoped for, though not necessarily to be believed in – Barry and Sam were introduced to each other at a 12-step rehab programme. Barry soon signed up to be his new friend’s sponsor and take him through the process, and felt energised by the similarities in their ambitions and worldview. “I think to find someone your own age, with the same dreams as you, from the same city and is also suffering from the same thing… we knew immediately that we could help each other,” recalls Sam. “You can lose your mind thinking about how rare that is.” However unsteady their respective circumstances may have been at the time, a brighter, more creative future suddenly came into focus. In between “secret” writing sessions the foundations of Bleech 9:3 were born, giving Barry and Sam purpose to move forward. “From the point of view of recovery and sobriety, we shared an intrinsic understanding of each other. It felt like we were building something very, very special,” says Barry…

This band was built on reimagining tradition, on honoring the old ways while pushing them someplace new." On their intoxicating new album, Thank the Lord...it's The Pink Stones, Pinkston and his bandmates do precisely that, offering up a joyful, adventurous take on '60s twang that blurs the lines between cosmic country, folk, bluegrass, soul, and psychedelic rock. Recorded once again with co-producer/engineer Henry Barbe (Drive-By Truckers, Deerhunter) in the band's hometown of Athens, GA, the collection showcases a more deliberate, mature side of The Pink Stones' sound, one that reflects all the personal and sonic growth that's defined the last few years for the hard touring five-piece. The songs on Thank the Lord... are humble and timeless, full of wry, sardonic wit and rich, evocative storytelling, and the performances are easygoing and amiable, with an effortlessly natural feel that belies the masterful craftsmanship behind them. The result is a record that wears its influences proudly on its sleeve, even as it subverts expectation, a work of poignant longing and playful humor that tips its cap to everyone from Merle Haggard and Earl Scruggs to Don Williams and The Byrds as it looks both forwards and backwards all at once. "A lot has changed since the last record," says Pinkston. "We've grown up, traveled all over the world, said goodbye to old bandmates…

events.description: Pynch are a true 21st century DIY band that have built up a dedicated global fanbase through a combination of tenacity, wistful lo-fi and life affirming lyricism. On their 2023 debut album, Howling at a Concrete Moon, they have followed through on their vision and delivered ten stunning tracks that offer a snapshot of what it is to be young and adrift at this strange junction of history. To record the album, the band enlisted Stereolab’s Andy Ramsay as Co-Producer and Tom Carmichael (Porridge Radio/Matt Maltese) as mixer who both helped to magnify and enhance Spencer’s home recordings while preserving their lo-fi aesthetic. The result is Pynch exactly as they were meant to be heard; intimate and introspective yet widescreen and danceable. Sonically, Pynch serve up a heady concoction of motoric beats (Julianna Hopkins), driving basslines (Scott Enock), soaring guitars (Spencer Enock) and melancholic synths (James Rees) to create a sound that is steeped in indie and electronic history yet still vitally present. In his lyrics, Spencer combines a yearning for meaning with dry observations about pop-culture, conspiracies and McDonalds; juxtaposing the celestial with the everyday, to the tune of a slacker Gameboy rhapsody. Since forming at university, Pynch have toured the UK and Europe, supported The Libertines, released their debut single on Speedy Wunderground and amassed over 3 million streams. With Howling at a Concrete Moon, they finally have an LP that captures this journey…

events.description: Prolific Scottish songsmith Tommy Ashby has spent his career refining a natural talent for capturing the innate beauty of everyday moments in a dulcet combination of ethereal sonics and hushed vocals. His fascination with the human relationship to sound saw him complete a PhD in Psychoacoustics, knowledge of which Tommy deftly utilises throughout his songcraft to illuminate the beautiful minutia of life, nature, and relationships. As his first self-produced effort, sophomore album ‘Mantis’ is understandably Tommy’s most introspective and personal work yet. A self-confessed over-thinker, Tommy uses the record to examine the anxieties and fears that arise through isolation and how our emotional connections and relationships to others can support us at our most vulnerable moments “The album name Mantis comes from the song of the same name, which is about the fear of making a real connection with someone. I liked the weird metaphor of a mantis, known for decapitating its potential mate. The idea is that we exaggerate the risks, and they hold us from doing what we should. The worry that if we put ourselves out there, our flaws will be on display for all to see. But opening ourselves up, even only a tiny bit, is the only way we make connections with others. Recorded live to analogue tape, it captures Danielle’s unmistakable voice, exceptional musicianship and honest songwriting at their very best. A former member of Trampled Under Foot and one of the most respected artists on today’s blues scene, Danielle Nicole has built an international following through her electrifying live performances and emotionally charged songs. Expect an unforgettable evening from an artist at the very top of her game.

Known for his powerful vocals and heart-on-sleeve songwriting, ADMT offers raw transparency in his music, aiming to normalise the conversation around mental health. Having famously sold out almost every show he has played: from building his craft busking on the streets to selling thousands of tickets, his sound, packed with R&B beats and massive pop hooks, is gaining legions of fans worldwide. ai.en: The Zac Schulze Gang play The Cluny, presented by DHP. The guitarist is known for precision and speed.

events.description: Guitarist Zac Schulze, is a world-class shredder, playing with precision, speed, and passion, but the focus of the trio isn't just his solos. The Zac Schulze Gang is an undeniable gang, a group unified by a like-minded sensibility that adds an electrifying charge to their rock'n'roll. Zac rides the thunder generated by the rhythm section of his drummer brother BenSchulze and bassist Ant Greenwell. The trio create a massive roar, all without losing sight of what matters most, the songs. The Zac Schulze Gang’s sound and work ethic harks back to the much-loved live dynamic and relentless touring schedules of 70s icons including Rory Gallagher and Dr Feelgood. Their unique sound also embodies elements of heritage classic rock acts like AC/DC and Thin Lizzy, while giving a nod to contemporary influences like Turnstile, Royal Blood and Queens of the Stone Age. The Gang have made lasting impressions at festivals including Eric Clapton's Crossroads, Planet Rock's Winter End in 2023 and Fairport's Cropredy Festival, and the Rory Gallagher Tribute Festival in Ballyshannon where the band first exploded onto the scene. Zac Schulze won Emerging Artist of the Year at the UK Blues Awards 2024 and followed this by winning Young Artist of the Year at the UK Blues Awards in 2025 and 2026. With sold-out concerts in the Netherlands, Germany, andthe UK, the Zac Schulze Gang are the band to watch.

ai.en: The Bones of J.R. Jones play The Cluny. The show looks back on the album Radio Waves, the sixth album by Jonathon Linaberry.

events.description: Jonathon Linaberry looks back on Radio Waves, his sixth album as The Bones Of J.R. Jones, but there’s more than just nostalgia at play. Recorded with producer Robbie Lackritz (Feist, Bahamas), the collection is moody and hypnotic, drawing on the sonic landscape of Linaberry’s youth as it reckons with the doubt and uncertainty of adulthood. The arrangements are entrancing, built on the tension between acoustic instruments and retro synthesizers, and Linaberry’s performances are raw and visceral, at times aching in their vulnerability. Put it all together and you’ve got a poignant exploration of memory and longing delivered by a relentless searcher, a revelatory work of personal reflection rooted in the endless beauty, pain, and chaos of growing up. Born in central New York, Linaberry got his start playing in punk bands before becoming enamored with the field recordings of Alan Lomax. He launched The Bones of J.R. Jones in 2012 and began releasing a series of albums and EPs that would land his songs in films and TV shows like True Detective, Suits, and Daredevil, and lead to countless tours across the US and Europe, including stops everywhere from Telluride Blues to Hardly Strictly Bluegrass. Along the way, Linaberry would also share bills with the likes of The Wallflowers, G. Love, and The Devil Makes Three, soundtrack an Amazon commercial helmed by Oscar-winning director Taika Waititi, and earn praise from Billboard, American Songwriter, Under the Radar, and more.

events.description: The Blues came calling first, but rock was always waiting around the corner. Well it would be, wouldn’t it? Coming from the deep south, it was inevitable, but living in the deep south of a major Yorkshire City, there’s a gritty hard edge to life! A female guitar prodigy, Chantel was told by a major label that she had a "great voice, but girls don't play guitar like that!" Wisely ignoring their comments, she enrolled at the Leeds College of Music and became the first student in the college’s history, to achieve a 100% pass mark at BTEC, with 18 distinctions. The Lurgan duo take Mississippi Hill Blues and Punk Rock and mix into their own unique dark Irish Punk Blues stew. The Bonnevilles are a no-frills guitar-and-drums two-piece from Ireland who play hard-hitting roots music they call "garage punk blues." Formed in Lurgan and Banbridge in 2009, the Bonnevilles feature guitarist and singer Andrew McGibbon, Jr. and drummer Chris McMullan. McGibbon was a blues fan whose take on the genre was turned upside down by R.L. Burnside's raucous collaboration with the Jon Spencer Blues Explosion, Ass Pocket of Whiskey. After checking out like-minded acts like the Immortal Lee County Killers and the Soledad Brothers, McGibbon decided to start doing some blues wailing of his own. Teaming up with McMullan, the group began playing out and in 2010 released their debut album, Good Suits and Fightin' Boots. As the band toured in support, both McGibbon and McMullan struggled with the death of a parent, which informed the duo's second LP, 2012's Folk Art and the Death of Electric Jesus. As the Bonnevilles continued to tour the U.K. and Europe, they shared stages with the likes of Bob Log III, the Black Diamond Heavies, T-Model Ford, and Kid Congo Powers. events.description: Berlin-based Swiss musician Anna Erhard is opening a new chapter in her career with the release of her new single,“1000 Sheep.” The track marks the beginning of the campaign for her forthcoming album of the same name, which is set for release in February 2027. Over recent years, Anna Erhard has established herself as one of the most distinctive voices in European indie pop. Her music lives somewhere between the laid-back spirit of Kurt Vile and the inventive charm of early Beck, blending distorted guitars and lo-fi keyboards with witty storytelling. Delivered with her trademark nonchalance, her songs transform everyday observations, travels and chance encounters into memorable musical snapshots. Following the release of her third studio album Botanical Garden in 2024, which was widely acclaimed across Europe, Erhard embarked on sold-out tours throughout the UK and performed extensively across the continent. Highlights of this period included an appearance at the legendary Glastonbury Festival as well as strong support from BBC6 Music, featuring heavy rotation airplay and several live sessions, including a recording at London's iconic Maida Vale Studios. With “1000 Sheep,” Anna Erhard offers a first glimpse into her forthcoming album and once again showcases her ability to turn everyday observations and fleeting encounters into witty, playful and captivating stories.

events.description: Happy 40th Anniversary to The Vaselines! "Wait a minute, didn't The Vaselines break up years ago?" Yes,The Vaselines did break up in 1989 in the week that their debut album 'Dum Dum' was released. "So they're getting back together again?" No, the Vaselines reformed in 2008 and went onto release two more albums, 'Sex With an X' on Sub Pop in 2009 and 'V For Vaselines' on their own label Rosary Music in 2014. "Are they any good?" OK, let me tell you everything! The Vaselines were formed in Glasgow in 1987 by singers/guitarists Eugene Kelly and Frances McKee, soon signing to The Pastels frontman Stephen Pastel's 53rd & 3rd label. They released two 12 inch singles 'Son of a Gun' and 'Dying For it' and one album 'Dum Dum'. Nirvana's Kurt Cobain regularly cited the Vaselines in interviews with the music press and Nirvana would go on to cover the Vaselines' ‘Molly's Lips’ and ‘Son of a Gun’ (both later compiled on their Incesticide collection) as well as perform ‘Jesus Doesn't Want Me for a Sunbeam’ on their legendary MTV Unplugged appearance which went on to introduce the band to a new world wide audience. Though they were not widely known outside the United Kingdom during their short career, their association with Nirvana brought them exposure, with Kurt Cobain describing Kelly and McKee as his "favourite songwriters in the whole world". Collaborating with Jordan Fish, the band has evolved beyond their early punk roots, seamlessly weaving organic rock riffs with electronic beats inspired by Nine Inch Nails, The Prodigy, and Gorillaz. Written during an isolated retreat in the French countryside, the ambitious record explores the complexities of wealth inequality, societal decay, and toxic escapism, yet it ultimately serves as a message of defiant hope and self-acceptance. events.description: Acclaimed musician, poet, director and actor Saul Williams tours his new album Leap Life, his first solo full-length in seven years. Moving between spoken word, jazz, hip-hop, ambient composition and ceremonial sound, the album finds Williams continuing his decades-long practice of using art as a transformative force. With 'Leap Life,' Williams expands the definition of what music itself can be. For nearly three decades, Williams has occupied a singular place in Black culture, resisting the confines of genre across music, literature and film to use art as a transformative device. He starred in Sinners which earned a record-breaking 16 Academy Award nominations; co-wrote and starred in the Sundance and Cannes award-winning SLAM, directed Neptune Frost, and has released numerous albums, books and multidisciplinary works. Combining powerful vocals, soaring melodies, driving rock and Celtic influences, the show takes audiences on a swashbuckling journey through a world of sky pirates, steam-powered airships, mythical creatures and forgotten cities. A specially created cinematic pirate movie unfolds on screen behind the band, bringing a thrilling treasure-hunt story to life through music, film and storytelling. And audiences are invited to join the adventure! Pirates, mermaids, Vikings, steampunk adventurers, wizards, witches and other fantasy folk are all welcome. Fancy dress is positively encouraged! HAZE Formed in Sheffield in 1978 by brothers Chris and Paul McMahon, Haze are veterans of the British progressive rock scene, having shared stages with the likes of Pallas, Pendragon and Solstice during the heyday of the 1980s neo-prog movement. Never content to be confined by genre, Haze blend progressive rock with folk, hard rock, metal, psychedelia and more, combining intricate compositions with an energetic, often unpredictable live performance. Now a genuine family affair, the band features Paul and Chris alongside drummer Danny McMahon and multi-instrumentalist Catrin Ashton on flute and fiddle. Their…

In 2027, Cardinal Black return to the road for their biggest headline tour to date, taking their new album, Second Sign of Life, across the UK, Ireland, Europe and North America. Released January 29th on Thirty Tigers, Second Sign of Life sees the Welsh-born trio stripping things back to their foundations; self-produced and self-engineered at Hamburg’s renowned Clouds Hill Studio between European tour dates, the record captures the instinctive chemistry of a band shaped by thousands of miles and countless shows together. That journey has already taken Cardinal Black from chart-topping records to sold-out shows at London’s Shepherd’s Bush Empire, New York’s Gramercy Theatre and Los Angeles’ Troubadour, as well as a standout Royal Albert Hall appearance with Peter Frampton. Now, with Second Sign of Life, the road opens up again. New songs, bigger rooms, and another chapter written night by night. events.description: Draw Out Your World is Caoilfhionn Rose’s fourth album and her first for Lost Map, to be released on February 5, 2027. Moving between intimate, quietly unfolding songs and driving, beat-led folktronica, it explores new motherhood, resilience through change and the work of turning imagined possibilities into a life of your own. Made with her husband and long-time creative partner Rich Williams, the album brings together ideas gathered over several years with songs written during pregnancy and early motherhood. Loops and fragments became starting points for sessions with friends: four tracks emerged from two days of improvisation in Copenhagen with Danish electronic jazz duo Svaneborg Kardyb, including the single ‘Horizon’. Elsewhere, keyboardist John Ellis helped older songs find new shapes, his rolling Fender Rhodes breathing fresh life into ‘Grow’. Just absolutely stunning, she´s an amazing artist Guy Garvey, BBC 6 Entrancing vocals and mesmeric instrumentation The Line Of Best Fit The sound is that of the first day of spring The Arts Desk Gorgeous, deeply immersive listening Clash Breathtakingly beautiful and intimately inspiring Atwood Magazine

ai.en: Nadav Tabak, a live looping guitarist, plays Cluny 2.

events.description: Nadav Tabak is a live looping guitarist who transforms a single acoustic guitar into a full-spectrum rhythmic and melodic experience. Using real-time looping, percussive techniques and layered instrumentation, he builds beats, basslines and soaring melodies live on stage — creating high-energy, immersive performances that blur the line between concert and dancefloor ritual. After a decade touring internationally as one half of the acclaimed guitar duo Opal Ocean, Nadav has stepped into his own solo chapter. His sound blends acoustic psy-trance, tribal grooves, Spanish rumba techniques and cinematic textures, moving fluidly between uplifting dance moments and atmospheric introspection. Each performance is improvised and shaped by the energy of the crowd, making every set unique. Growing up in Auckland, New Zealand, Nadav developed an experimental mindset that now defines his solo project. Armed with a looping pedal and a deep rhythmic sensibility, he constructs intricate compositions in real time, drawing from global influences and organic percussion. His self-titled debut EP, released in 2023, showcases this fusion of technical precision and emotional depth. Nadav toured extensively across Europe, performing at festivals and sharing stages with world-class artists. Highlights include opening for Manu Chao at Chez Narcisse (Val-d’Ajol), Hilight Tribe at l’Autre Canal Nancy, Delgres and Rootsriders at the Olympia in Paris, as well as performing at Earth Garden Festival in…

events.description: Gavin Fairhall Lever are a stunning explosion of colour in the wild and unruly garden of the London folk scene. A tangle of roots from Northern Ireland, Cornwall and Norfolk gives exuberant life to a truly contemporary folk music, full of thorns and flowers. The trio bring together the exhilarating, joyful tumble of Celtic trad, a melodic warmth, vibrant rhythmic invention, and the subtle expressivity of jazz harmony. Tunes unfold like stories, with dynamic and textured arrangements keeping the pages turning, from chapters of luminous stillness into passages of unstoppable drive. All performed with a compelling combination of fire, precision and mongrel bite. The trio have become renowned for their captivating live performances (“flawless” - FolkLondon), including at Caceres Irish Fleadh (Spain), Zilleghem Folk (Belgium), Broadstairs Folk Festival, and Celtic Connections Glasgow. Following on from the success of their debut record (“One of my top favourites of the year... Brilliant.” - RnR ****), their second album Tearing Down Walls was recorded live to tape at Analogue Catalogue Studios in Northern Ireland with Julie McLarnon (Lankum, Alasdair Roberts, Brian Eno), and released to acclaim in February 2025. “Thoroughly thrilling” - Songlines ****, “Breathtaking musicianship” - RnR ‘An exhilarating mashing together of Celtic and Eastern European traditional music and jazz harmony.. ai.en: The Ruts, 50 Years of Ruts Music 1977 to 2027, play The Cluny, presented by AGMP Concerts.

events.description: The Ruts '50 Years of Ruts music 1977-2027' In 1977, The Ruts emerged from London with a sound unlike anybody else around them - the raw urgency of punk colliding with reggae, dub and rock, driven by formidable musicianship and a fierce sense of purpose. With Malcolm Owen, Paul Fox, Dave Ruffy and Segs Jennings, The Ruts created a body of music whose power has endured far beyond its original moment. The Singles: In A Rut. Babylon’s Burning. Something That I Said. Jah War. Staring At The Rude Boys. West One (Shine On Me). The Album: The Crack: One of the defining British punk albums of its era: urgent, inventive, politically aware and musically fearless. These songs became part of the fabric of British punk -- and a sound that refused to stay within punk’s boundaries. After losing Malcolm Owen in 1980, the remaining members chose integrity over nostalgia by re-inventing themselves as Ruts DC, eventually losing the legend that was Paul Fox in 2007 But the story does not end there. Ruts DC remain a living, evolving band to this day. But the time has come to celebrate the whole story… RUTS DC present: 50 YEARS OF RUTS MUSIC - 1977-2027 These shows are about taking the music that exploded out of a movement and bringing it onto a stage in 2027 with all its urgency and relevance intact. Music made across five decades — from The Crack and Grin & Bear It, through Animal Now, Rhythm Collision, Music Must Destroy, and Counterculture? “This ain’t no nostalgia trip, it’s a celebration”…

ai.en: Kirsten Adamson and The Tanagers play Cluny 2. Adamson is an award-winning Scottish singer-songwriter.

events.description: Award-winning Scottish singer-songwriter Kirsten Adamson has built a reputation for emotionally direct songwriting, soaring vocals and heartland Americana folk-rock. The daughter of Big Country and Skids frontman Stuart Adamson, she has steadily carved out a musical identity entirely her own, drawing comparisons to Sandy Denny, Emmylou Harris and Kate Bush. Following the release of Dreamviewer in 2025, Adamson and her band The Tanagers have toured extensively across the UK and Europe, with festival appearances and support slots culminating in a major UK tour opening for The Proclaimers in autumn 2026. Their forthcoming album, Live In London, captures the band at The Water Rats after several years spent developing their sound together on the road. Its release is followed by a major UK headline tour in spring 2027, marking the beginning of the next chapter for Kirsten Adamson & The Tanagers.

With harmonies, macabre humour and folkloric storytelling, their music conjures the romance of old cafés, the spirit of New Orleans porches, and the intimacy of campfire songs, with touches of macabre humour and familiar folklore tales. Formed from a journey through New Orleans, busking festivals across Europe, and intimate campfire shows in England, Around About Dusk bring warmth, charm, and authenticity to every stage. events.description: Sound of the Sirens are a singer-songwriting duo based in Exeter, Devon comprising of Abbe Martin & Hannah Wood. Honing their craft over the past decade, Martin & Wood have cemented themselves as firm favourites as “one of the UK’s finest folk acts” not only on the Westcountry scene, but nationally, and internationally too. Their status, and fast-growing fan-base is not only testament to the pair’s prowess as songwriters and musicians, but as people too. Martin & Wood are two of the hardest working musicians on the scene and wear their hearts very much on their sleeves in terms of their songwriting. The pair glide gracefully through laments of past relationships, and life experiences, as well as highlighting the important topics of the day, namely mental health awareness, and homelessness. Without being pigeonholed into any stereotypical genre, the instrumentation of the band is vast, and varied. Martin (stage right) plays acoustic and high-strung (Nashville tuning) guitar, mandolin, and bass drum, while partner in crime Wood (stage left) plays acoustic and electric guitar, tambourine, snare drum, and the piano. The pairs’ musical and vocal dexterity dovetail beautifully on the co-written songs, which range from beautiful, emotive ballads, to up-beat, foot stomping, hands in the air, sing-along anthems. The dynamic duo and their musical creations translate very well onto recorded media, but it is in the live arena where the pair truly excel. There is a certain majesty about…

SJM Concerts & Live Nation Present Supergrass plus support Monday 26th April 2027 NX Newcastle Formed in Oxford in 1993, Supergrass are one of the UK's most celebrated and enduring bands. Across six studio albums, the band have produced a string of iconic tracks including ‘Alright’, ‘Caught By The Fuzz’, ‘Mansize Rooster’, ‘Lenny’, ‘Going Out’, ‘Richard III’, ‘Sun Hits The Sky’, ‘Pumping On Your Stereo’, ‘Moving’ and ‘Grace’. Their debut album I Should Coco reached Number 1 in the UK and has sold over a million copies worldwide, followed by five further acclaimed studio albums including In It For The Money, Supergrass, Life On Other Planets, Road To Rouen and Diamond Hoo Ha. Supergrass have received a BRIT Award and Ivor Novello Award, alongside six Top 10 albums and 10 Top 20 singles. Following their split in 2010, the band reunited in 2019 for a hugely successful world tour, returning to the stage to play to fans across the UK and internationally. With their celebrated catalogue and reputation as one of Britain's great live bands, Supergrass will return to UK stages in 2027 for a series of headline shows.

In 2024, Bec O’Malley went on a hike in the Peak District with his friends. He’d taken his acoustic guitar with him and decided to film a quick video of him covering Dylan Gossett’s ‘Coal’ while out on the misty paths. In the short clip, the young musician forgets the words a few lines in, but there was something about it that connected with those who saw it on their algorithm. Perhaps it was the unpolished charm of the video – mistake left in, cut off before he could try again – or his resonant vocals that hit in even just a few seconds, or a combination of the two. The likes quickly poured in, more so than for any other video he’d posted on TikTok before, igniting interest in this unknown talent. O’Malley’s name may have been undiscovered when that video was posted, but by that point, he’d already been playing music and writing his own songs for years. Growing up in Stockport, he first picked up a guitar aged 12, learning the basics from his cousin and fleshing out the rest from YouTube tutorials. A few years later, his interest turned from simply playing others’ creations to working on his own, first in bands with school friends, and then on his own. Sheffield’s own soul-swaggering trio, Lightning Threads deal in grit, groove, and rhythm. At core, a band that lives for the push and pull of authentic live music: squeezed through valve amps and carried by raw collective moments. Tom Jane (guitar/vocals) slinging riffs and licks which veer from melodic subtle moments to searing solos. Locking down the low-end groove is Sam Burgum (bass/vocals), providing the glue and the bounce all at once. Then Hugh Butler (drums/keys) shifts between thunderous backbeats and textured organ parts, creating a much bigger sound than you might expect. You can hear the DNA straight away — the late ‘60s British blues explosion runs right through us. Bands like The Doors, Rory Gallagher, Santana, Cream, Hendrix, Zeppelin, Peter Green's Mac, Free — that raw, exploratory energy where blues met volume. But we’re just as shaped by the electric blues artists that came before them — B.B. King, Muddy Waters, Howlin' Wolf, Sister Rosetta — who were the originators of that emotional weight and storytelling. And then there’s the modern torchbearers: SRV, Gary Clark Jr., Kingfish, Marcus King, Bonamassa, Samantha Fish, DeWolff, Fantastic Negrito — artists who’ve taken that tradition and kept it alive into the present day. Somewhere in the middle of all that is where we sit — we're not trying to recreate it, but to carry it forward, with our own stamp on it. Standing at the crossroads of the future and the past, you’ll find Marcus Trummer. He is an artist who dares to draw outside the lines, pushing the definitions of traditional genres while still honouring the legacy of his influences. Known for combining blues, soul, R&B, and rock, the singer-songwriter and guitarist from Calgary, Canada, released his debut album ‘From The Start’ in 2024. The ten-song record earned him a nomination for Blues Artist of the Year at the 2025 Western Canadian Music Awards. More recently, he was named Male Blues Vocalist of the Year at the 2026 Canadian Blues Music Awards. Beyond Canada, Trummer is quickly establishing an international presence. In 2023, he won the Telluride Blues Challenge, and the following year, made his U.S. debut at the renowned Telluride Blues & Brews Festival. In May 2026, he played Moulin Blues Festival in the Netherlands, marking his first performance in Europe. With a guitar amplifier turned up loud and wearing his heart on his sleeve, Trummer can be found on stages around the world. His soulful approach to music and life resonates with audiences of all ages and backgrounds.

The members of the band now are: Greg Griffin (vocals and guitar) Paul Newsome (vocals, guitar) Nathan Birkett( Bass), Tony Auton ( guitar), and Richard Stuverud (drums). Manchester’s Proud Mary combine the angst, sourness and romance of those working class bands before them - the Smiths, James, Oasis, and the Stones Roses - and define themselves, like their counterparts did, with music. They formed in 1999 and took their name from the familiar Creedence Clearwater Revival song without really wanting to take over the world like some of their peers. The four-piece, which is comprised of singer Greg Griffin, guitarist Paul Newsome, slide guitar player Adam Gray, and bassist Nev Cottee, aimed to make decent rock & roll with the passion of rhythm & blues, the diversity of space rock, and with simplicity of mid-'60s pop music. Oasis' Noel Gallagher took to their strict dose of heavy rock, and made them his first signing to his Sour Mash label. "Very Best Friend" marked their debut single in April 2001, and studio full-length entitled “The Same Old Blues” followed in June. They caught national appeal within the U.K. with top ten hit record “The Same Old Blues” before playing various shows across England during summer 2001 and for the next few years touring with, Oasis , Ocean Colour Scene, The Black Crowes, Paul Weller, Neil Young, Ryan Adams and Stereophonics' successful festival gigs at A Day at the Races in Donington and Cardiff.
